correctness.rationale: An exact edge-crossing formula and a factor-two antipodal wall-jump calculation at each vertex yield a planar sign-balance condition. The finite sign-jump lemma forces paired opposite projected neighbor directions, and convexity turns those local pairings into complete centrally symmetric edge-belt polygon boundaries. Conversely every edge-disjoint belt contributes two section crossings, so the theorem follows for all generic normals. The standalone integer/Q(sqrt5) verifier was run and passed all 2,680 exact nondegenerate normal checks and edge-cycle checks for three examples. Finite checks support examples, not the universal implication.

value.rationale: A complete necessary-and-sufficient structural criterion for fixed central-section side count reduces infinitely many section directions to finitely many vertex incidences or central polygon edge belts. It derives exact equisection counts for three canonical polytopes, includes a genuinely distinguishing counterexample to projection-equiprojectivity, and is useful for future classification and slice combinatorics. This is substantially more than a one-off numeric example or a routine edge counting identity.
